title: Validated issue identity type with an alias staging bridge
description:
Introduce the validated issue-id type and the temporary bridge that lets each layer adopt the `IssueId` name while the workspace stays green.

## Background

Issue ids are `String` throughout: `Issue.id` and `Issue.dependencies` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:414,427`), `MinimalIssue.id` (`:670`) and `MinimalBlockedIssue.id` (`:758`). No `IssueId`, short-id or prefix type exists. Flipping `Issue.id` directly to a newtype produces 293 type errors in 32 library files before the binary, the server and the tests are reached, so adoption happens layer by layer behind an alias. About 79 `format!` sites and 136 `#[error]` attributes interpolate ids, so the newtype's `Display` must print exactly the id.

Every stored id in this repository (issue records, dependency lists, the index, events and gate runs) is a canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID produced by `IdAuthority::uuid_at` (`repository_state/mutation.rs:149-162`). `uuid` parsing also accepts simple, braced, URN and uppercase forms, so canonical decoding needs an explicit check. `InputsDigest` (`domain/repository_inputs.rs:345-403`) is the crate's newtype precedent. The short id is the first `SHORT_ID_LENGTH` (`domain/types.rs:24`) characters of the id.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A new `domain::identity` module defines the validated issue-id newtype, which accepts only the canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID form and rejects simple, braced, URN, uppercase and empty input with an error naming the input.
- [hard] REQ-02: The newtype serializes and deserializes as a plain JSON string, and its published JSON schema is `{"type":"string"}`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The newtype implements exactly `Display` (printing the same text as `as_str()`), `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `PartialOrd`, `Ord`, `Hash`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize` and `JsonSchema`, plus the methods `as_str()` and `short_id() -> &str`; `short_id()` returns the first `SHORT_ID_LENGTH` characters. It implements no `Deref`, `Borrow<str>` or comparison with strings.
- [hard] REQ-04: `crate::domain::identity::IssueId` is a temporary alias for `String`, and a temporary `IssueIdStaging` trait implemented for `String` provides `short_id()` with the same result as the newtype.
- [hard] REQ-05: Property tests show that canonical ids round-trip through parsing and serde unchanged, and that each non-canonical spelling of the same UUID is rejected.

## Notes

The alias and trait are a named temporary bridge (`@/inv/canonical-cutover`, `@/inv/convention-convergence`). A later change in this epic gives the newtype the `IssueId` name and deletes both, so until then the newtype carries a staging name. Imports use the module path `crate::domain::identity::IssueId`, which stays the same across that change.

planning.outcome: A validated issue-id newtype with a fixed trait set exists beside a temporary String alias.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One new pure module with its property tests and no consumer change.

title: Graph node traits expose dependency ids as string views
description:
Let the graph traits yield dependency ids as borrowed string views, so a node can store typed ids without changing the graph algorithms.

## Background

`GraphNode::dependencies(&self) -> &[String]` (`crates/jit/src/graph/mod.rs:45-51`) and `HierarchyNode::dependencies` (`graph/hierarchy.rs:158-168`) force each implementor to store a `Vec<String>`. Implementors are `Issue` (`domain/types.rs:814`), `EdgeView` (`graph/hierarchy.rs:493`), `ProspectiveNode` (`commands/template_expand.rs:457`), whose placeholder ids are `__apply_placeholder__:{role}` (`:435`), and the test nodes `TestNode` (`graph/mod.rs:585`), `PropNode` (`graph/hierarchy.rs:1106`) and `FixtureNode` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/hierarchy_vectors_test.rs:41`), which read non-UUID ids such as `r-t1` from the hierarchy test vectors. Placeholder and vector ids are not issue ids, so the traits stay independent of the issue-id type. The MSRV (1.97) supports return-position `impl Trait` in traits.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GraphNode::dependencies` and `HierarchyNode::dependencies` return an iterator of `&str` instead of a slice of `String`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each implementor compiles against the new signature without changing the type of the ids it stores, and placeholder and test-vector nodes keep their non-UUID ids.
- [hard] REQ-03: The existing graph property tests pass with unchanged assertions.

planning.outcome: GraphNode and HierarchyNode yield dependency ids as borrowed string views.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One trait signature change with six mechanical implementor adaptations.

title: Graph queries return nodes rather than id strings
description:
Make the graph's id-returning queries return references into the node set, so a typed caller reads the id from the node instead of parsing a string.

## Background

`DependencyGraph` returns owned id strings: `compute_transitive_reduction -> HashSet<String>` (`crates/jit/src/graph/mod.rs:442`), `find_shortest_path -> Vec<String>` (`:475`) and `find_redundant_edges -> Vec<(String, String)>` (`:519`). `GraphError::NodeNotFound { id: String }` (`:61`) names a dangling reference. Callers sit in `graph/hierarchy.rs`, `commands/dependency.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`, `validation/graph.rs`, `validation/repository.rs` and `main.rs`. Once nodes store typed ids, a caller handed a `String` would have to rebuild an id from it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `compute_transitive_reduction`, `find_shortest_path` and `find_redundant_edges` return references to nodes of the graph (or ids borrowed from them), not owned strings.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each caller reads ids from the returned nodes, and no caller rebuilds an id from a string the graph produced.
- [hard] REQ-03: `GraphError::NodeNotFound` names the missing reference for display only, and no caller converts it into an id.
- [hard] REQ-04: `HierarchyConfig::membership_closure` (`graph/hierarchy.rs:296`) returns node references, and `MembershipDivergence.issue_id` (`:575`) holds the node's own id type.
- [hard] REQ-05: Graph property tests pass with unchanged assertions.

planning.outcome: Graph queries return node references, so callers never reparse an id string.

title: Id prefixes parse once into an IssueIdPrefix
description:
Type the input and output of issue-id prefix resolution, so a user-supplied prefix is parsed once and resolves to an `IssueId`.

## Background

`IssueStore::resolve_issue_id(&self, partial_id: &str) -> Result<String>` (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:191`) takes raw input. On their full-length fast paths the JSON backend (`storage/json.rs:1264-1268`) and the memory backend (`storage/memory.rs:849-853`) pass that raw input to `load_issue`. `MIN_ID_PREFIX_LENGTH` lives in storage (`storage/errors.rs:251`), and `storage/reference.rs:56` const-asserts `SHORT_ID_LENGTH >= MIN_ID_PREFIX_LENGTH`. One shared pure resolver owns prefix normalisation, minimum length and matching; this change keeps that behaviour and types its signature.

The shared resolver's contract fixes two error classes. A prefix that normalises below the minimum length fails with `InvalidIdPrefixError` (`storage/json.rs:1274`, `storage/memory.rs:858`), refined to `INVALID_ID_PREFIX` (`output.rs:1163`), before any record is read, as `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/short_hash_tests.rs:84,399`, `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/issue_status_projection_tests.rs:350`, `the removed exit-code subprocess suite:1220,1372` and `storage/reference.rs:742` assert. Input of well-formed length that lies outside the id alphabet, such as `nonexistent`, or matches no issue is reported as not found with exit code 3, as `cli_issue/error_json_tests.rs:26`, `the removed exit-code subprocess suite:57`, `cli_issue/top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs:87`, `cli_issue/quiet_mode_tests.rs:188` and `cli_repo_workflow/workflow_tests.rs:438` assert. Where this description and the landed resolver contract differ, the resolver contract governs. Production callers of `resolve_issue_id` sit in `main.rs` and in `commands/claim.rs`, `commands/issue.rs`, `commands/document.rs`, `commands/gate.rs`, `commands/graph.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`, `commands/item.rs`, `commands/archive.rs` and `commands/mod.rs`. The settled boundary is that only the CLI and server entry points parse and resolve prefixes. So that this change can land green before that boundary exists, each of these callers parses its input where it calls the resolver. These call-site parses are a named temporary bridge: later changes in this epic move parsing to the CLI and server entry points, retype the command methods to take resolved ids and delete each call-site parse, and the bridge is gone when no production `IssueIdPrefix` parse remains outside those entry points.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `domain::identity::IssueIdPrefix` is the parsed form of user-supplied id input. It applies the resolver's normalisation and minimum-length rules, and it owns `MIN_ID_PREFIX_LENGTH`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The shared prefix resolver and `IssueStore::resolve_issue_id` take `&IssueIdPrefix` and return `IssueId`, and each `IssueStore` implementation, test wrappers included, implements the retyped method.
- [hard] REQ-03: `IssueIdPrefix` implements an infallible `From<&IssueId>`, because a full id is a valid prefix.
- [hard] REQ-04: Input that normalises below `MIN_ID_PREFIX_LENGTH` fails at parse with the invalid-prefix error before any record is read. Input of sufficient length that is outside the id alphabet or matches nothing is reported as not found with exit code 3. The listed not-found tests and invalid-prefix tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-05: Neither backend passes unparsed user input to `load_issue`, and a full-length prefix resolves through the same resolver as a short one.
- [hard] REQ-06: Both storage backends pass the shared prefix-resolution conformance tests.
- [hard] REQ-07: Each call-site parse this change adds sits at an existing production `resolve_issue_id` call and is the only interim parse; no new caller of the resolver is introduced.

planning.outcome: Prefix resolution maps a parsed IssueIdPrefix to an IssueId through the one shared resolver.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One type plus one retyped resolver with one-line caller adaptations.

Short ids are truncated by length at `commands/graph.rs:326,588` and `commands/batch_create.rs:339`, and `commands/batch_create.rs:409` builds a placeholder short id with `"0".repeat(SHORT_ID_LENGTH)`. `commands/template_expand.rs` carries ids of the issues an apply creates. Integration tests call `add_dependency` about 120 times, nearly all with `&String` arguments.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No struct field, enum field or function parameter in `commands/dependency.rs`, `commands/graph.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/template_expand.rs` or `commands/batch_create.rs` holds an issue id as `String`, `&str` or `Vec<String>`; each uses `IssueId`. Template placeholder ids, which are not issue ids, keep their own type.
- [hard] REQ-02: Executor methods in this family take `&IssueId` and resolve no prefixes, with one exception: dependency removal takes `&IssueIdPrefix` and matches it against the issue's own dependency list, so a dangling dependency can still be removed. Callers that hold full ids, such as templates, batch creation and tests, pass them directly.
- [hard] REQ-03: Dependency removal matches its prefix through the shared resolver over the issue's dependency ids, and no hand-written prefix match remains in this family.
- [hard] REQ-04: Callers of dependency removal pass `IssueIdPrefix`: the CLI parses the user's argument into one without resolving it, and callers that hold an `IssueId` convert it through `IssueIdPrefix::from(&IssueId)`.
- [hard] REQ-05: Short ids in this family come only from `short_id()`, and no site truncates an id by length.
- [hard] REQ-06: No production `IssueIdPrefix` parse and no production `resolve_issue_id` call remains in this family's files.
- [hard] REQ-07: Code in this family, its unit-test modules included, uses issue ids only through `as_str()`, `short_id()`, `Display`, `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`/`Eq`, `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, `Hash` and serde, so it compiles unchanged once `IssueId` is the validated newtype.

## Notes

`crate::domain::identity::IssueId` is at this point an alias for `String`, and the `IssueIdStaging` trait gives it `short_id()`. Retyping to the alias is compiler-neutral, so this change is checked by its criteria rather than by type errors; a later change replaces the alias with the validated newtype and the compiler then reports any site missed here. Parameters are retyped outside-in: the CLI and server entry points already resolve ids, and callers in this family are retyped before the functions they call in inner layers.

planning.outcome: Label-coverage assertions decode into a typed configuration with a compiled pattern.
